policy: semantic events are canonical; provider adapters may map them only after current official hook syntax is verified

session.start.purpose: load canonical policy pointer and minimal project fingerprint

task.route.purpose: resolve smallest capability set and context budget

before.tool.purpose: block obvious destructive/credential-risk actions and enforce task-scoped tools

after.tool.purpose: record compact evidence or metrics without dumping raw tool output into memory

before.compact.purpose: persist only durable task state and decisions

after.test.purpose: capture pass/fail evidence and route remaining failures

task.complete.purpose: verify requested outcome and persist only durable discoveries

providerMapping.claude: adapter-required; verify current native hook names before rendering
providerMapping.gemini: adapter-required; verify current native hook names before rendering
providerMapping.qwen: adapter-required; verify current native hook names before rendering
providerMapping.kimi: prefer skills/plugins and canonical policy; do not invent unsupported hooks
providerMapping.codex: use native capabilities only when verified; otherwise semantic events remain advisory
providerMapping.cursor: provider rule integration only when verified
providerMapping.hermes: orchestrator may implement semantic lifecycle events directly
